title: Workforce HRMS & Desktop App
shortDesc: An internal HR platform for a growing company: attendance, leave, payroll and approvals in one place, plus a desktop app for Windows and macOS. Internal tool, so described at a high level.
longDesc: A rebuild of the company's workforce system into a full HRMS: a Next.js admin and employee portal on MongoDB, and an Electron desktop app for Windows and macOS. Built by a two-person team, with me as the senior developer. Internal to the company, so this page describes the engineering approach rather than the product specifics.
theProblem: An older workforce system had accumulated issues and fixed rules. Numbers disagreed between views, and because payroll depends on attendance, every inconsistency turned into a money problem.
theMessyPart: Real attendance is messy: different shifts, machines that restart or drop offline, and rules that vary by team. All of it has to resolve to one consistent number everywhere, because payroll consumes it.
architecture: A Next.js and Node.js application on MongoDB with per-person logins and a role- and department-scoped permission model, an approval engine, and ledger-style balances. An Electron desktop app for Windows and macOS stores data locally and syncs reliably when the connection returns. Everything is self-hosted and deployed through scripted, health-checked releases with automatic rollback.
technicalDecisions:
1. Configurable policy: rules live in admin settings with defaults that preserve existing behaviour, not in code.
2. Ledger-style balances instead of mutable counters, so history is always explainable.
3. Approved payroll data is locked; reopening requires a recorded reason.
4. Resumable report generation so large reports survive interruptions.
5. Audit trails with reasons for every sensitive change, and notifications to the people affected.
6. Offline-tolerant desktop app that keeps pending data until the server confirms receipt.
7. Automated tests and in-app help kept in step with every release.
whatIdChange: I would model shifts and rosters before building attendance reporting. Retrofitting varied schedules onto a single-shift assumption forced rework across reports and payroll.
fullContent:
## Scope

An internal HR platform in three parts: an **admin portal** for HR and management, an **employee portal**, and a **desktop app** for Windows and macOS, all backed by one Next.js, Node.js and MongoDB system that I also host and operate.

It covers attendance and shifts, leave, payroll, incentives, reimbursements, employee records and reporting, with approvals that can span multiple levels per request type.

## The engineering themes

- **Policy as configuration.** Almost nothing that HR cares about is hard-coded. New rules ship as settings whose defaults keep today's behaviour, so features can be introduced gradually.
- **Correctness first.** Balances are ledgers, approved payroll is locked, and every sensitive change is audited with a reason.
- **Resilience.** The desktop app keeps working offline and syncs safely; long-running reports resume where they stopped.
- **Maintainability.** A large automated test suite, searchable in-app help in all three apps that is updated with every release, and scripted deployments with automatic rollback.

## Note

This is an internal company system built by a two-person team, with me as the senior developer. There is no public link and I have kept the description deliberately general.
